المشكلة/نتيجة الفحص: تأكد السبب من قراءة الكود: كروت «تأخر رد المورد» و«المفاوضات المفتوحة» تعد صفوف BookingVendor، بينما جدول المتابعة يعرض Bookings. الكروت قد تضاعف الحجز متعدد الموردين وتضم حصصًا تابعة لحجز ملغي، وروابطها تفتح الجدول بلا فلتر المؤشر. وقت القياس كان كل كارت 6 حصص تخص 5 حجوزات، والجدول 4 حجوزات. الرقم 4 خاص بهذه البيانات وليس قاعدة دائمة.

تاريخ آخر تحقق: 2026-09-05

<details>
<summary>برومبت الإصلاح الجاهز</summary>

Use AGENTS.md and treat the following contract as proposed until the product owner approves it, because docs/specs/01_PRD.md is missing. Implement a shared GetNegotiationMonitorQueryAction returning a Booking builder and reuse it in LateVendorResponsesWidget, AdminDashboardHeaderWidget, AdminDashboardSectionsWidget, and BookingsMonitorResource. Count distinct bookings, never BookingVendor rows. Late = booking lifecycle vendor_review or customer_review AND at least one vendor allocation pending with non-null response deadline strictly before one captured UTC asOf. Open = same booking lifecycle AND at least one vendor allocation pending or modified, without a deadline condition. Exclude timed_out and all other vendor statuses; exclude every booking lifecycle outside the two review statuses. Add negotiation_scope=late|open table filters and make each card URL reproduce its exact query. Evaluate count and linked result at the same UTC instant; do not require late and open totals to match and do not hardcode the observed 4. Keep authorization at the Filament/policy boundary, public ULIDs, bilingual labels, and no tenancy. Add isolated Pest tests for multi-vendor distinct counting, future/overdue pending, modified, timed_out, accepted/rejected, cancelled/completed, null/equal/earlier deadlines, UTC equivalence, cache freshness, card-to-filter equality, localization, and authorization. Do not mutate production or install dependencies there. Report product assumptions, files, before/after fixture counts, and focused test output.

</details>

records.title: VTSE-001 — P0 — Cross-vendor service resubmission and unrestricted mass assignment
records.body:
**Trigger:** an approved vendor submits `POST /api/v1/vendor/services/{service:public_id}/resubmit` for another vendor's service that has an open change request.

**Evidence:**

- [ServiceResubmitFormRequest.php](../../app/Modules/Catalog/Http/Requests/ServiceResubmitFormRequest.php#L11) authorizes every request and accepts arbitrary `changed_fields`.
- [ServiceResubmitController.php](../../app/Modules/Catalog/Http/Controllers/ServiceResubmitController.php#L20) passes the route-bound service and payload directly to the Action.
- [ServiceResubmitAfterChangesAction.php](../../app/Modules/Catalog/Application/Actions/ServiceResubmitAfterChangesAction.php#L26) does not compare the service owner with the authenticated vendor; line 45 updates the model with the submitted map.
- [Service.php](../../app/Modules/Catalog/Domain/Models/Service.php#L79) makes ownership, category, product type, price, currency, and other fields fillable.

**Impact:** a vendor can modify another vendor's service and can change ownership, category, product type, price, translations, or other fillable values. This combines IDOR with mass assignment.

**Required regression:** two vendors and one foreign service; the attacker must receive a non-enumerating 404, and submitted non-allowlisted fields must never change.

records.title: VTSE-002 — P1 — Customer payment read IDOR and internal identifier exposure
records.body:
**Trigger:** any authenticated account requests a known payment ULID belonging to another customer.

**Evidence:** [Payments customer routes](../../app/Modules/Payments/Routes/customer.php#L13) require authentication only; [ShowPaymentController.php](../../app/Modules/Payments/Http/Controllers/Customer/ShowPaymentController.php#L16) queries by `public_id` without owner scope; [PaymentResource.php](../../app/Modules/Payments/Http/Resources/PaymentResource.php#L23) returns internal `booking_id`.

**Impact:** cross-customer payment status and amount disclosure, plus violation of the public-ULID API rule.

**Required regression:** customer B must get 404 for customer A's payment; vendor/admin behavior must be explicit; the response must use the booking public ID.

records.title: VTSE-003 — P1 — API booking items snapshot zero commission
records.body:
**Trigger:** a customer adds a published service through the booking API, then payment is captured.

**Evidence:** [AddItemToBookingAction.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Application/Actions/AddItemToBookingAction.php#L94) writes `commission_bps` as `0`; [CalculateCommissionAction.php](../../app/Modules/Settlement/Application/Actions/CalculateCommissionAction.php#L44) treats any non-null snapshot, including zero, as authoritative and skips the configured resolver.

**Impact:** the platform commission can become zero and the entire captured amount can accrue to the vendor. Category-specific commission resolution is also not proven through this path.

**Required regression:** create an API booking under a known 1500 bps rate, capture payment, and assert the persisted snapshot, commission, vendor share, and balanced ledger.

records.title: VTSE-004 — P1 — Multi-item refund reverses excessive commission and has two reversal paths
records.body:
**Trigger:** a full or partial payment refund where the payment covers multiple booking items.

**Evidence:** [ProcessRefundAction.php](../../app/Modules/Payments/Application/Actions/ProcessRefundAction.php#L93) directly reverses the first commission using the complete refund amount, then emits `RefundCompleted`; [ReverseCommissionOnRefundCompletedListener.php](../../app/Modules/Settlement/Application/Listeners/ReverseCommissionOnRefundCompletedListener.php#L80) applies the same full amount to every commission; [ReverseCommissionAction.php](../../app/Modules/Settlement/Application/Actions/ReverseCommissionAction.php#L39) divides the full refund by each item's gross and does not cap reversal to the remaining vendor/platform amounts.

**Impact:** vendor balances and commission receivables can be over-reversed. The first commission can also have its state advanced twice even where the ledger idempotency key suppresses a duplicate ledger group.

**Required regression:** two items with different totals, partial and full refunds, retry of the event, and assertions that each reversal is capped and aggregate debits equal the refunded allocation exactly once.

records.title: VTSE-005 — P1 — Completed refund can call the gateway again
records.body:
**Trigger:** an API refund completes successfully, then a `REFUND` webhook or queue retry processes the same refund.

**Evidence:** [ProcessRefundAction.php](../../app/Modules/Payments/Application/Actions/ProcessRefundAction.php#L41) locks the refund but has no completed-state guard before marking it processing and calling the gateway; [ProcessPaymobWebhookAction.php](../../app/Modules/Payments/Application/Actions/ProcessPaymobWebhookAction.php#L78) can enter that path.

**Impact:** duplicate gateway refund attempt or a valid completed refund being overwritten as failed.

**Required regression:** replay a completed refund and assert one gateway call, one ledger group, and a permanently completed state.

records.title: VTSE-006 — P1 — Payment initiation lacks booking-state and prior-payment guards
records.body:
**Trigger:** the owner initiates payment for a draft, cancelled, empty, already paid, or already pending booking.

**Evidence:** [InitiatePaymentController.php](../../app/Modules/Payments/Http/Controllers/Customer/InitiatePaymentController.php#L28) checks ownership; [InitiatePaymentAction.php](../../app/Modules/Payments/Application/Actions/InitiatePaymentAction.php#L22) immediately calls the gateway and creates a payment without checking booking lifecycle/payment state or an existing payable attempt.

**Impact:** invalid-state payments and duplicate gateway intents.

**Required regression:** table-driven tests for draft, cancelled, confirmed-unpaid, confirmed-paid, empty, and duplicate-pending bookings.

records.title: VTSE-007 — P1 — Captured webhook amount is not reconciled with the payment
records.body:
**Trigger:** Paymob sends a successful capture event with an amount or currency different from the local payment.

**Evidence:** [ProcessPaymobWebhookAction.php](../../app/Modules/Payments/Application/Actions/ProcessPaymobWebhookAction.php#L102) invokes capture without validating the parsed captured amount; [CapturePaymentAction.php](../../app/Modules/Payments/Application/Actions/CapturePaymentAction.php#L46) posts the full local payment amount.

**Impact:** the system can mark and ledger more money than the gateway actually captured.

**Required regression:** mismatched amount/currency must fail closed, preserve the payment state, and create no capture ledger.

records.title: VTSE-008 — P1 — Duplicate PaymentCaptured delivery can inflate amount paid
records.body:
**Trigger:** a queued listener succeeds in updating the booking then is retried, or the same event is delivered twice.

**Evidence:** [UpdateBookingPaymentStatusListener.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Application/Listeners/UpdateBookingPaymentStatusListener.php#L20) increments `amount_paid_minor` without an event or payment deduplication record.

**Impact:** the booking can appear overpaid and transition incorrectly.

**Required regression:** handle the same captured payment event twice and assert an unchanged amount and state on the second delivery.

records.title: VTSE-009 — P1 — Two settlement paths can pay one withdrawal twice
records.body:
**Trigger:** the weekly settlement batch and the admin mark-paid flow read the same approved withdrawal before either updates it.

**Evidence:** [SettlementRunAction.php](../../app/Modules/Settlement/Application/Actions/SettlementRunAction.php#L29) reads approved withdrawals without a row lock and uses `wd_settle_batch:{id}`; [MarkWithdrawalPaidAction.php](../../app/Modules/Settlement/Application/Actions/MarkWithdrawalPaidAction.php#L42) checks state before its transaction and uses `wd_settle:{id}` near line 100.

**Impact:** two valid ledger groups can represent the same payout. The batch path also marks paid without the bank proof, transfer reference, admin identity, and audit evidence required by the manual path.

**Required regression:** interleave both paths for one withdrawal and assert a single transition, ledger group, proof policy, and payout reference.

records.title: VTSE-010 — P1 — Direct vendor modification is born expired
records.body:
**Trigger:** vendor uses `POST /vendor/booking-vendors/{id}/modify`, then the customer tries to accept.

**Evidence:** [VendorModifyBookingAction.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Application/Actions/VendorModifyBookingAction.php#L77) creates a pending modification without `expires_at`; [CustomerConfirmModifiedBookingAction.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Application/Actions/CustomerConfirmModifiedBookingAction.php#L77) rejects null expiry as expired.

**Impact:** the API reports a created proposal that the customer can never accept.

**Required regression:** create through the vendor HTTP route, accept through the customer HTTP route before expiry, then reject after expiry.

records.title: VTSE-011 — P1 — Vendor modification bypasses paid/cancelled booking guard
records.body:
**Trigger:** vendor modifies a booking after payment or customer cancellation.

**Evidence:** [VendorModifyBookingAction.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Application/Actions/VendorModifyBookingAction.php#L48) does not call `PreventModificationAfterPaymentAction` or validate the parent lifecycle before moving the booking to customer review.

**Impact:** a paid or cancelled booking can re-enter negotiation.

**Required regression:** paid, partially paid, refunded, cancelled, completed, and active-state cases through the HTTP route.

records.title: VTSE-012 — P1 — Accepted add-item modification trusts vendor payload and misses required snapshots
records.body:
**Trigger:** vendor proposes a newly added item and customer accepts it.

**Evidence:** [VendorModifyRequest.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Http/Requests/VendorModifyRequest.php#L28) accepts broad item data; [AddBookingModificationItemAction.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Application/Actions/AddBookingModificationItemAction.php#L110) lets payload product type override the service; [CustomerConfirmModifiedBookingAction.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Application/Actions/CustomerConfirmModifiedBookingAction.php#L221) creates a booking item without proving service ownership/publication/price and omits required snapshot/status fields from the booking-item schema.

**Impact:** foreign or unpublished service, fabricated price/type, database failure, or incomplete financial/tax/commission snapshots.

**Required regression:** all three product types plus foreign, unpublished, changed-price, missing-field, and wrong-type cases.

records.title: VTSE-013 — P1 — Modification preview computes the wrong quantity delta
records.body:
**Trigger:** item quantity changes, with or without a unit-price change.

**Evidence:** [BookingModificationDiffService.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Application/Services/BookingModificationDiffService.php#L79) calculates `(newPrice - oldPrice) * oldQuantity` instead of `newPrice * newQuantity - oldPrice * oldQuantity`.

**Impact:** customer approval is based on a displayed delta different from the applied booking total.

**Required regression:** old `1 × 100`, new `3 × 200`, expected delta `500`; include quantity-only and price-only cases.

records.title: VTSE-014 — P1 — Removing an item through an accepted modification leaves inventory reserved
records.body:
**Trigger:** customer accepts a proposal that removes a rental or sale item.

**Evidence:** [CustomerConfirmModifiedBookingAction.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Application/Actions/CustomerConfirmModifiedBookingAction.php#L233) deletes the booking item without releasing or changing its `service_inventory_reservations` row.

**Impact:** phantom held/confirmed inventory blocks later customers.

**Required regression:** remove rental and sale items and assert the linked reservation is released in the same transaction.

records.title: VTSE-015 — P1 — Vendor can decide a customer-cancelled booking
records.body:
**Trigger:** customer cancels during vendor review, then vendor accepts, rejects, or modifies its still-pending allocation.

**Evidence:** [CancelBookingByCustomerAction.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Application/Actions/CancelBookingByCustomerAction.php#L48) changes the booking but does not close vendor allocations; [VendorAcceptBookingAction.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Application/Actions/VendorAcceptBookingAction.php#L40), [VendorRejectBookingAction.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Application/Actions/VendorRejectBookingAction.php#L41), and [VendorModifyBookingAction.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Application/Actions/VendorModifyBookingAction.php#L57) validate allocation state/deadline without rejecting the cancelled parent.

**Impact:** a cancelled booking can be mutated or potentially confirmed after cancellation.

**Required regression:** cancellation followed by each vendor decision; all must fail atomically and preserve cancellation.

records.title: VTSE-016 — P1 — Unlimited sale stock is treated as zero
records.body:
**Trigger:** add a sale service whose `stock_quantity` is null, where null represents unlimited stock.

**Evidence:** [AddItemToBookingAction.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Application/Actions/AddItemToBookingAction.php#L170) converts null to zero before subtracting held quantity, while the catalog inventory path treats null as unlimited.

**Impact:** valid unlimited-stock products cannot be booked.

**Required regression:** null stock succeeds; finite stock still rejects only when the requested quantity exceeds availability.

records.title: VTSE-017 — P1 — Service-create API accepts inactive or wrong-type categories
records.body:
**Trigger:** approved vendor submits rental/sale/digital service creation with an existing category that is inactive or excludes that product type.

**Evidence:** [CreateRentalServiceRequest.php](../../app/Modules/Catalog/Http/Requests/CreateRentalServiceRequest.php#L46) validates category existence only; the corresponding sale and digital requests use the same pattern. The Filament selector filters categories, so UI and API enforce different rules.

**Impact:** invalid catalog classification and services that cannot be managed consistently.

**Required regression:** every product type against allowed, excluded, inactive, and missing categories.

records.title: VTSE-018 — P1 — Legacy vendor fulfillment page bypasses fulfillment guards
records.body:
**Trigger:** vendor advances an item from `VendorActiveBookingsPage`.

**Evidence:** [VendorActiveBookingsPage.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Filament/Vendor/Pages/VendorActiveBookingsPage.php#L127) and line 178 call `MarkBookingItemStateAction` directly instead of guarded fulfillment Actions.

**Impact:** unpaid, cancelled, or refunded work may be marked complete; completion evidence and `BookingItemFulfilled` aggregation can be skipped.

**Required regression:** the page must reject unpaid/refunded/cancelled bookings and use the same evidence/event behavior as the API Actions.

records.title: VTSE-019 — P1 — Item completion does not complete the parent booking
records.body:
**Trigger:** every item reaches its per-type terminal fulfillment state.

**Evidence:** [AggregateBookingVendorSubStatusListener.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Application/Listeners/AggregateBookingVendorSubStatusListener.php#L48) completes the vendor allocation and emits `BookingVendorCompleted`; no consumer of that event aggregates all vendors into `bookings.fulfillment_status` or invokes [CompleteBookingTransition.php](../../app/Modules/Booking/Domain/States/BookingLifecycleStatus/Transitions/CompleteBookingTransition.php#L20).

**Impact:** parent bookings can remain active/not-started, `BookingCompleted` does not fire, and downstream loyalty/review eligibility is stranded.

**Required regression:** multiple vendors and mixed product types; complete the last item and assert exactly one parent completion event and lifecycle transition.

records.title: VTSE-020 — P2 — HTTP idempotency key is not scoped to actor and operation
records.body:
**Evidence:** [IdempotencyKeyMiddleware.php](../../app/Modules/Payments/Http/Middleware/IdempotencyKeyMiddleware.php#L25) looks up the supplied key without a complete actor/route scope and does not atomically reserve it before downstream execution.

**Impact:** a key reused by another actor/route can return an unrelated response; concurrent first requests can both reach the gateway.

**Required regression:** same key across users/routes and two concurrent requests; only the matching actor/operation may replay.

records.title: VTSE-021 — P2 — Ledger idempotency accepts a different financial payload
records.body:
**Evidence:** [PostLedgerTransactionAction.php](../../app/Modules/Settlement/Application/Actions/PostLedgerTransactionAction.php#L236) compares transaction kind and currency only when reusing a key, not accounts, directions, amounts, or related entity.

**Impact:** accidental reuse can silently return a ledger group for different money movements.

**Required regression:** same key/kind/currency with changed entries must throw a payload-mismatch exception.

records.title: VTSE-022 — P2 — Customer modification decision lacks operation idempotency
records.body:
**Evidence:** [Booking customer routes](../../app/Modules/Booking/Routes/customer.php#L30) do not apply idempotency middleware to the decision endpoint. Static checks inside the Action do not provide an externally scoped idempotency result for concurrent duplicate submissions.

**Impact:** duplicate decisions can race and repeat transitions/events.

**Required regression:** concurrent accept and accept/reject conflict with one persisted decision and one event chain.

records.title: VTSE-023 — P2 — Paymob failure detail is discarded
records.body:
**Evidence:** [PaymobGateway.php](../../app/Modules/Payments/Infrastructure/Gateways/PaymobGateway.php#L113) parses a failure code, but [ProcessPaymobWebhookAction.php](../../app/Modules/Payments/Application/Actions/ProcessPaymobWebhookAction.php#L119) uses the previous payment failure value instead of the webhook DTO value.

**Impact:** failures collapse to `unknown`, reducing support and reconciliation evidence.

**Required regression:** known gateway failure code maps to the expected persisted bilingual failure reason.

records.title: VTSE-024 — P2 — Vendor category endpoint ignores vendor product approvals
records.body:
**Evidence:** [VendorCategoryController.php](../../app/Modules/Catalog/Http/Controllers/Vendor/VendorCategoryController.php#L21) calls the public category list Action rather than the vendor-scoped Action.

**Impact:** vendors see active categories for product types they are not approved to sell, producing inconsistent UI/API choices.

**Required regression:** a rental-only vendor must not receive sale-only/digital-only categories.

records.title: VTSE-025 — P2 — Settlement-run history is disconnected from the settlement command
records.body:
**Evidence:** [SettlementRunAction.php](../../app/Modules/Settlement/Application/Actions/SettlementRunAction.php#L27) processes withdrawals and returns counters but never creates or updates [SettlementRun.php](../../app/Modules/Settlement/Domain/Models/SettlementRun.php#L13). Repository references show settlement-run records created only by development seeding/factories and displayed by Filament.

**Impact:** the weekly command can pay withdrawals while the admin settlement-run screen has no corresponding period, totals, status, or audit record.

**Required regression:** one command run must create one run record with bounded period, totals, final status, and traceable included withdrawals.

records.title: VTSE-D01 — Suspended customer access
records.body: `EnsureAccountIsActive` is not consistently applied to Booking, Payments, Reviews, and Settlement customer route groups. Decide whether suspended customers may read existing orders while being blocked from new booking, payment, review, and wallet mutations. Then enforce and test that matrix.

records.title: VTSE-D02 — Payment endpoint roles
records.body: Payments customer routes require authentication but not `role:customer`, unlike neighboring customer modules. Decide whether admins/vendors may intentionally initiate or view customer payments through these endpoints. Keep ownership checks mandatory regardless of that decision.

records.title: P1 — Add Governorate then City or Area dependency to search.
records.body: The search sidebar previously exposed one unscoped City field, accepted city without governorate outside planner mode, and never passed governorate into the search contract. Added separate Governorate then City controls backed by the existing Geography API: City is disabled until a governorate is selected, receives only that governorate's active cities, clears stale values on parent change, and preserves both values on query-string reload. Web validation now requires the parent for a city and rejects mismatched pairs. `SearchServicesDTO` and the existing database fallback now apply governorate coverage (primary location or covered city) together with the city filter; governorate searches intentionally use the established SQL path instead of expanding the Meilisearch index in this ticket. No migration or stored-data rewrite was required. Evidence: focused Pest 4 tests / 28 assertions, successful Vite production build, and Playwright Chromium 2 tests passed (setup plus English desktop and Arabic mobile dependency/filter flow).

records.title: P1 — Filter vendor options by selected Occasion and Category.
records.body: The vendor select previously listed every approved vendor with any published service, regardless of the selected occasion/category. `VendorBrowsingRepository::approvedForFilter()` now requires one published service whose category (including parent-category selection) and linked occasion satisfy both active filters. The search controller removes an invalid submitted vendor instead of applying a stale choice, and the existing sidebar JavaScript refreshes options immediately from server-derived vendor/service combinations whenever either parent changes. No route, taxonomy, migration, or stored-data rewrite was added. Evidence: focused Pest 3 tests / 24 assertions for the vendor and geography filters, successful Vite production build, and Playwright Chromium 2 tests passed (setup plus English desktop and Arabic mobile dynamic vendor options, including stale selection clearing).

records.title: P3 — Rename and move the rating filter.
records.body: Renamed the existing filter to `Vendor Rating` / `تقييم المورد` and moved its existing markup directly below Vendor, before Price. The `min_rating` parameter, options, selection and backend semantics are unchanged. Evidence: focused Pest passed (3 tests, 15 assertions), Pint and `git diff --check` passed, and Playwright passed the filter label, adjacent group order, value selection and viewport bounds on English desktop and Arabic mobile while retaining the dependent-vendor regression (2 tests including setup). No route, database or asset changes.

records.title: P2 — Add a stable vendor slug URL.
records.body: The profile already had a unique, protected slug and ULID identity, but the public controller accepted only ULIDs and generated links ignored the slug. Public Blade vendor links now prefer the existing slug, approved profiles resolve by slug or ULID, and legacy ULID paths return a 301 redirect retaining query parameters. API/model route identity remains ULID; profile name edits cannot change the protected slug. Registration retains the existing name-plus-ULID-suffix strategy and bounds new slugs to the existing 160-character column, including duplicate and long names. No migration, old-slug rewrite, or data deletion. Evidence: combined gallery/slug/type/registration Pest passed 49 tests / 340 assertions, focused PHPStan passed with no errors at 512MB, Pint and `git diff --check` passed. Playwright passed actual legacy-link redirects, generated-link clicks, name-edit continuity, and EN desktop/AR mobile flows (3 tests including setup and type regression).

records.title: P2 — Show a vendor-only public slider.
records.body: The public Blade page did not render the profile's existing `portfolio` media. It now renders only the active vendor's media, uses available large/thumb conversions with original-file fallback, and reuses the existing gallery interaction for thumbnails and wrapping Previous/Next buttons. Empty galleries are hidden; a single image has no unnecessary controls. Narrowed the existing vendor-hero CSS selector so it cannot darken the new gallery heading. No new package, media collection, schema, or production upload. Evidence: the 49-test / 340-assertion combined Pest run includes ownership and zero/one/multiple-image coverage in both locales; Vite build passed with existing runtime-resolved asset notices; Playwright's final 3-test run passed actual image loading, keyboard and pointer navigation, ownership isolation, empty/single galleries, stable links, and viewport bounds. Screenshots were visually inspected at `tests/e2e/.results/vendor-gallery-en.png` and `vendor-gallery-ar.png`. Initial browser failure was isolated to local E2E media fixture placement because `public/storage` is a directory rather than a link; only test fixture placement was adjusted, not application storage settings or user files.

records.title: P1 — Count and show only service types with real services.
records.body: The page previously counted approved type grants even without published services. The existing browsing repository now groups that vendor's displayable services across all pages, and the Blade type badges, type count, service count/list, and vendor index search/count use the same published-service scope. Deleting the last service of a type removes its badge and decreases both counts; drafts and other vendors do not contribute. The scope supports `catalog.digital_services_enabled`; DIG-01 now defaults this switch to false for the current phase; tests explicitly enable digital when verifying all three types. No service records or subscriptions were changed. Evidence: combined Pest passed 49 tests / 340 assertions, including EN/AR and digital enabled/disabled, 13 rentals spanning pagination, sale deletion, and approved-only empty state. Focused PHPStan/Pint and `git diff --check` passed; final combined Playwright passed 3 tests, and a separate digital-disabled Playwright run passed 2 tests including setup and real deletion/reload/count checks.

records.title: P2 — Make event end date and time optional.
records.body: The database and resources already supported null ends, but the wizard HTML/JavaScript, planner search, draft requests, and DTO required them; parsing a missing end would otherwise substitute the current time. The wizard and EN/AR copy now mark end optional, keep future start required, reject malformed or nonpositive supplied ranges, and pass null unchanged through web/API requests, DTO and persistence. Offset dates are stored in UTC. Rentals retain a concrete per-item inventory window using their existing stored positive default duration only when no explicit item/event end exists; the event end remains null. Missing rental defaults are rejected with localized guidance, not invented durations. The same fallback covers customer-accepted rental additions; vendor conflict warnings use the saved item end and include active reservations without an attached item. No schema/data migration or old-record rewrite. API request/resource examples, registry and Bruno draft request were updated. Evidence: final focused Pest passed 53 tests / 248 assertions across EN/AR, rental/sale/digital, omitted/null/empty end, explicit end, invalid ranges, UTC, overlapping inventory, modification additions and vendor warnings. Focused PHPStan passed with no errors at 512MB; Pint and `git diff --check` passed; Vite build passed with existing asset notices. Playwright passed 3 tests including setup, existing checkout and actual start-only search/checkout in EN desktop and AR mobile for all three types; stored null and rental windows were checked against the isolated database. Screenshots `tests/e2e/.results/planner-optional-end-en.png` and `planner-optional-end-ar.png` were inspected. Earlier E2E API-cookie authentication failure was corrected in the test without weakening auth; the new vendor warning regression exposed and fixed the existing SQL NULL exclusion.

records.title: P2 — Replace the Who is calling field with Notes.
records.body: Replaced the actual storefront "Who is celebrating?" field with a localized multiline Notes textarea. The existing `booking_customer_notes` text table now receives notes through a customer-owned, transaction-protected append action reused by draft creation and cart additions; identical latest notes are deduplicated, changed notes append without overwriting history, and failed service additions roll back note writes. Legacy celebrant columns and records remain intact. Browsing-only wizard submission uses the new web `POST wizard/context` flow to retain notes in the session without exposing private or long text in search URLs; successful checkout clears that session context. Cart, customer booking detail, booking API resources, and the owning vendor's detail/decision pages show escaped multiline notes. Validation accepts up to 10,000 characters and rejects longer input without truncation or partial writes. No new package, schema migration, or old-record rewrite. Existing API request/resource documentation, registry, Bruno example, and Discovery code map were updated. Evidence: final focused Pest passed 73 tests / 395 assertions, including EN/AR, 10,000-character preservation, oversized rejection, exact API round-trip, append history, rollback, customer/vendor ownership, and escaped script text. Focused PHPStan passed on 14 files at 512MB; Pint and `git diff --check` passed; agent-doc validation passed (7 documents, 69 local links, 17 modules). Combined Playwright passed 4 tests including setup, actual rental/sale/digital wizard submissions, multiline notes surviving cart reload, and search-session persistence in both locales. The final vendor-specific Playwright rerun passed 2 tests including setup and EN desktop/AR mobile multiline rendering; screenshots `tests/e2e/.results/vendor-event-notes-en.png` and `vendor-event-notes-ar.png` were inspected. Browser verification exposed unavailable Filament whitespace utility styling; applying pre-wrap only to the escaped note content fixed both collapsed lines and template-indentation spacing. Planner textarea screenshots were also inspected before the vendor rerun reset test artifacts. Focused evidence is complemented by the final local regression matrix below; production acceptance is not claimed.

records.title: P1 — Render matching packages inside search results.
records.body: Consolidated the existing `PackageRecommendationReader` output into one package section inside `.sf-search-results` for both category and planner contexts, removed the duplicate hero rendering, preserved the current query context, and retained the existing category/occasion scoping. No schema, routing, or data changes were required. Evidence: focused Pest passed (3 tests, 12 assertions), Vite production build passed, and Playwright passed in English desktop and Arabic mobile (2 tests). Geography, date, and availability constraints remain explicitly scoped to PKG-04.

records.title: P1 — Repair package card selection.
records.body: Package cards now open a public, localized details route keyed by the package ULID, show the translated description and Brick Money-formatted budget, and continue to the existing planner with the package occasion preselected. Missing or unpublished packages return to search with an accessible localized error instead of failing silently. No schema changes or synthetic service relationships were added. Evidence: focused Pest passed (5 tests, 25 assertions), route discovery and PHP syntax checks passed, Pint passed after its one import-order fix, `git diff --check` passed, and Playwright passed the real card click and next-step link in English desktop and Arabic mobile (2 tests including setup).

records.title: P1 — Add an Occasion-dependent Package filter.
records.body: Added Package immediately after Occasion in the search sidebar, backed by the existing `PackageRecommendationReader` and package ULIDs. The server exposes only published packages linked to the selected occasion, rejects stale cross-occasion selections, and narrows the rendered package cards when one package is selected. The browser refreshes the options immediately and clears the prior value whenever Occasion changes; no second taxonomy or API endpoint was introduced. Evidence: focused Pest passed (7 tests, 39 assertions), Pint passed, Vite production build passed (with the repository's existing runtime-resolved asset notices), and Playwright passed card selection plus the dependent filter behavior in English desktop and Arabic mobile (3 tests including setup).

records.title: P1 — Reorder the homepage party builder and remove Category there only.
records.body: The homepage quick builder now renders Occasion → Governorate → City/Area → Date and Time, removes Category only from this form, loads active governorates from the existing geography repository, and reuses the established city endpoint and dependency behavior so City stays disabled and is cleared until a Governorate is selected. The date control now captures `event_starts_at` with `datetime-local`, and all valid values arrive selected on the existing search page. Evidence: focused Pest passed (4 tests, 33 assertions), Pint passed, and Playwright passed actual dependent-city loading and form submission in English desktop plus Arabic mobile (2 tests including setup). The first E2E attempt was invalidated only by test-factory country duplication; after binding the fixture to the seeded country, the rerun passed.

records.title: P1 — Integrate packages into the search backend.
records.body: Package recommendations now derive their eligible category IDs from the exact canonical service-search database query, so they inherit published lifecycle, text, product type, category, occasion, vendor, governorate/city coverage, price, rating, and rental availability constraints instead of maintaining parallel filter SQL. Exact event start/end timestamps are used for overlap checks when supplied; date-only searches retain day-level behavior. Packages are then constrained to occasions linked to the matching service categories, and a selected package is shown only when still eligible. Evidence: focused Pest passed (11 tests, 69 assertions), Pint passed, Playwright passed package click/filter plus deterministic city and availability changes (4 tests including setup), `git diff --check` passed, and focused PHPStan passed with no errors at 512MB. The first PHPStan attempt was incomplete only because the configured 128MB worker limit was exhausted; the higher-memory rerun completed cleanly.

records.title: P2 — Display a fixed package price as one EGP amount.
records.body: Package recommendation reads now expose a single `fixed_budget` only when the stored minimum and maximum minor-unit values are equal, using Brick Money for the one-time minor-unit conversion. Homepage, search, and package-detail cards render that amount once without From/To wording while preserving range and starting-price behavior for non-fixed packages; homepage cards also use the public package-details route. Evidence: focused Pest passed (6 tests, 41 assertions), the complete package Playwright spec passed in both locales and across filtering/availability scenarios (4 tests including setup), Pint passed, focused PHPStan passed with no errors at 512MB, and `git diff --check` passed.

records.title: P2 — Add optional vendor social and website URLs.
records.body: Added nullable Facebook, website, and Instagram URL columns through a module migration, then wired them through registration rules/DTO/action, API profile reads/updates, and vendor/admin profile forms. Empty strings normalize to null, omitted update fields remain unchanged, explicit null clears a link, and invalid links are rejected before registration or profile mutation. Labels and URL feedback are localized in EN/AR; Scribe field/response examples, the API registry, and Bruno examples cover the changed contract. Evidence: focused registration/social/profile Pest passed (24 tests, 208 assertions), the final social regression rerun passed (10 tests, 106 assertions), Pint passed, focused PHPStan passed (including the final update-action check with `--debug` after a parallel-worker timeout), and Playwright passed real registration plus profile editing/reload in both locales (3 tests including setup). The migration was verified on isolated test databases; deployment still needs the normal migration step. Earlier browser attempts exposed test timeout/locale setup and verification-fixture errors, all corrected before the green rerun.

records.title: P1 — Require a valid vendor phone number.
records.body: The request and registration action already required an E.164 phone, but the Filament regex incorrectly accepted a zero country-code prefix. All three entry points now share the same E.164 regex, with localized required/invalid/duplicate messages. Phone normalization removes separators only from string input, so malformed non-string requests return validation errors without a cast warning. Regression tests prove missing, empty, local-only, zero-prefix, short, long, and malformed inputs cannot create a user or profile; valid spaced numbers still register. Evidence: focused registration/social Pest passed (40 tests, 287 assertions), Pint passed, focused PHPStan passed with `--debug` and 512MB, PHP request syntax and `git diff --check` passed, and Playwright passed invalid-phone feedback followed by corrected registration and profile editing in EN/AR (3 tests including setup).

records.title: P1 — Enforce vendor approval before portal access.
records.body: The existing API `vendor.approved` middleware and operational-page guard were not consistently applied to the vendor service surface: the services list, category browser, and resource access checks could still be reached directly before approval, and the onboarding checklist linked pending vendors to an unavailable service operation. These entry points now require `VendorOperationalAccess` (approved profile plus verified email and phone); stale product-type grants cannot bypass the profile gate. Pending, rejected, and changes-requested vendors receive 403 for service operations and the API returns the structured `vendor_approval_required` error; approved but unverified vendors receive `phone_verification_required`. Profile, documents, business-hours, coverage and phone-verification pages remain available for completing onboarding. Evidence (2026-10-05): focused approval/portal Pest passed 17 tests / 188 assertions for pending, rejected, changes-requested, approved and approved-unverified states in EN/AR; the related category/sale/price regressions passed 106 tests / 1,382 assertions. Scoped PHPStan passed with no errors; Pint and `git diff --check` passed. Actual Playwright passed setup plus one EN desktop/AR mobile scenario covering direct URLs and onboarding preservation. No migration or stored-data rewrite; final local regression evidence is recorded below.

records.title: P2 — Support vendors without a company.
records.body: The existing Individual business type is now labeled `Individual / No company` in EN/AR. Vendor profile editing exposes the same three domain types as registration, updates the selected type, and dynamically requires only its applicable legal fields; admin editing follows the same visibility rules. Hidden stored legal values are preserved rather than cleared, and no placeholder company records or schema changes were added. Evidence: focused profile/social Pest passed (16 tests, 211 assertions), Pint passed, and Playwright passed registration, Individual/Company field switching, save and reload in EN/AR (3 tests including setup). `git diff --check` passed.

records.title: P2 — Remove City from initial vendor registration.
records.body: Removed City from the initial Filament registration form while keeping Governorate required. Shared request/action rules now accept a missing/null city; the DTO preserves null rather than casting it to zero. Legacy API callers may still submit a city, and mismatched governorate-city pairs remain rejected. The existing vendor profile page keeps City required for completion. The column was already nullable, so no migration or data rewrite was needed. API registry, request PHPDocs and Bruno now describe the nullable initial city. Evidence: focused registration/social/profile Pest passed (51 tests, 411 assertions), Pint passed, focused PHPStan passed with no errors, and Playwright passed city-free registration followed by selecting City in the profile and saving in EN/AR (3 tests including setup). `git diff --check` passed. Approval ordering is tracked separately in REG-03/REG-06.

records.title: P1 — Complete profile and documents after approval.
records.body: The existing approval action still requires the full eligibility checklist, while approved vendors can edit profile, account, documents, hours and coverage from the same portal session. The gap was the dashboard checklist hiding itself immediately after approval, which removed the resumable path for post-approval document/profile work and first-service setup. `VendorOnboardingChecklistWidget::canView()` now reuses the existing checklist for approved vendors and remains visible while any actionable step is incomplete; service operations remain behind `VendorOperationalAccess` and the approval/eligibility rules are unchanged. Evidence: focused `VendorApprovalPortalAccessTest` passed 8 tests / 149 assertions in EN/AR, including pending/rejected/changes-requested denial, onboarding-page preservation, approved catalog access, and an approved vendor with unfinished setup seeing the resumable checklist. No migration or stored-data rewrite; no registration restart is required.

records.title: P2 — Replace raw keys on vendor dashboard cards.
records.body: The rental/sale/digital cards generated `vendor-portal.dashboard.services_by_type.*` keys that had no translations; added nonempty EN/AR labels for all three without changing their underlying counts or financial calculations. Recent-booking status badges now use the existing `booking.vendor_status.*` translations instead of deriving English text from enum values; filled the missing English `timed_out` label. Regression tests reject raw keys/state names, check all vendor-status translations, and render actual cards and a timed-out booking in both locales. Evidence: combined focused Pest passed 19 tests / 161 assertions including the static Filament translation gate and document lifecycle regressions. Pint and PHP syntax checks passed; `git diff --check` passed. Filament paths remain excluded by the configured PHPStan, so no widget PHPStan coverage is claimed. Actual Playwright dashboard journey passed in EN desktop/AR mobile, verified one service of each type, the localized status, no exposed translation/state keys, and no page-wide horizontal overflow. `tests/e2e/.results/vendor-dashboard-labels-en.png` and `vendor-dashboard-labels-ar.png` were inspected. No route/schema/package change; Digital visibility is handled by DIG-01.

records.title: P1 — Repair the vendor documents navigation route.
records.body: Reproduced an actual 404 on the correctly generated `/vendor-portal/vendor-documents-page` URL: each row eagerly called `GenerateDocumentSignedUrlAction` while rendering, so one missing private file aborted the entire list and generated unnecessary signed-link audit entries for ordinary page reads. The existing Filament View action now invokes that same ownership/path/expiry-checked action only on explicit activation, redirects to the signed URL for an existing file, and reports a localized unavailable-file notification for 404 without breaking the table. Other HTTP failures, including forbidden access, are not swallowed. The existing route, page slug, panel middleware, vendor-only query, private file storage and approval lifecycle remain unchanged; no replacement file/data or new route was invented. Evidence: final focused Pest passed 19 tests / 161 assertions across navigation, guest/customer denial, owned/foreign row isolation, missing-file handling, explicit owned-file open and single audit write, private-path safeguards, document lifecycle/upload, dashboard labels and translation coverage. Pint, PHP syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed; focused PHPStan passed for the existing signed-URL action at 512MB, not the excluded Filament page. Final combined Playwright passed 3 tests including setup and actual EN desktop/AR mobile dashboard/documents journeys. The documents test clicked the native language switch and navigation, verified RTL/LTR and own-only records, activated the unavailable-file action, then reloaded the direct route with 200. Screenshots `tests/e2e/.results/vendor-documents-en.png` and `vendor-documents-ar.png` were inspected. Earlier browser attempts exposed isolated-factory geography duplication and locale/sidebar setup races; the final run uses seeded geography, the real language switch, and waits for its existing sidebar initialization before a normal click. Cross-reference: `BUG-VDOC-001` in the earlier 73-record ledger; no unrelated old records or totals were closed. Final local suite evidence is recorded below; production acceptance is not claimed.

records.title: P1 — Enforce phone verification after approval.
records.body: Approval requires a phone number and verified email; approved vendors must verify their phone before operations or receiving-booking APIs, while profile/documents/hours/coverage and verification remain reachable. Identity now binds the real SMS Misr adapter outside local/testing, with five-minute hashed codes, five-guess limit, atomic single use, random staging/production codes and localized provider failures. No schema, credentials or production settings changed. Evidence: approval lifecycle/portal Pest 17 tests / 188 assertions, Chromium approval journey 2 tests with approved-unverified access in EN/AR, and SMS gateway/phone page Pest 12 tests / 44 assertions covering success, replacement, expiry, replay, wrong phone, guess limits, provider rejection, missing credentials, password-reset separation and environment bindings. Real delivery remains a deployment check requiring SMS Misr credentials and approved sender, not an unimplemented binding.

records.title: P2 — Remove four nonrequired properties from customer service detail.
records.body: Removed Location from the customer detail's booking facts, vendor preview and attribute component, and removed Made to order, Perishable and Stock from the sale attributes. Empty attribute sections and empty booking-fact groups are no longer rendered. Stored detail values and the stock-based disabled booking button are preserved. Evidence: final focused purchase/account/loyalty/search Pest passed (25 tests, 149 assertions), Pint and `git diff --check` passed, and Playwright passed rental/sale/digital detail pages plus sold-out empty-state rendering in English desktop and Arabic mobile (2 tests including setup). No route, schema or stored-data change. An initial render failure exposed the remaining vendor-preview reference, which was removed before the green rerun; the persistence test was corrected to compare database-hydrated values on both sides.

records.title: P2 — Define the Vendor to Occasion relationship.
records.body: Product accepted service/category-derived eligibility: `occasion_category` maps occasions to categories, and public/vendor eligibility is derived through active displayable services rather than a direct vendor↔occasion pivot. No schema or stored-data change was required; existing search/package/category tests cover the relationship.

records.title: P1 — Enforce Main Category then Subcategory.
records.body: The existing shared category/occasion concern now supplies dependent main/subcategory fields to all three vendor resources. Main choices are active, type-compatible roots; the disabled subcategory field becomes available only after selecting a main category, shows its active/type-compatible direct children, and clears on parent changes. Server-side form rules reject missing, mismatched, nested-main, inactive, soft-deleted and wrong-type categories during both create and edit. Main category is form-only; the existing persisted category ID stores the selected child, with no new schema/API/DTO contract. Edit forms hydrate the pair; historical root-category services are not reclassified when opened, show EN/AR guidance, and require a valid child before saving. Actual edit validation revealed a separate 403: the vendor session guard selected a different permission namespace from the seeded web permissions. Service policy helpers now explicitly use the existing web namespace, and own-service checks also require the actor's vendor profile to own the record. Foreign edit URLs remain non-enumerating 404s and users without update permission remain forbidden. Evidence (2026-10-05): combined focused Pest passed 64 tests / 717 assertions, including 51 category/authorization cases, sale access, translation coverage, catalog security and Excel regressions. Pint and PHP syntax checks passed; focused PHPStan passed for the changed ServicePolicy (Filament paths remain excluded), and git diff --check passed. Combined actual Playwright passed 3 tests including setup and the existing sale access journey; the category journey created, edited and reloaded six services across rental/sale/digital, EN desktop and AR mobile using native form controls, and verified cleared stale children and refreshed occasion guidance. All six tests/e2e/.results/vendor-category-pair-{rental,sale,digital}-{en,ar}.png screenshots were inspected. The repaired full-marketplace journey includes a real subcategory linked to Birthday and passed through service publication and payment creation. Final regression evidence is recorded below. Category selection does not rewrite historical application data.

records.title: P1 — Accept and display service prices in EGP.
records.body: The existing native Filament price boundary remains the source for rental/sale/digital prices and now the booking invoice path renders the stored minor-unit values without re-conversion. Added a printable admin invoice route with service lines, vendor delivery, governorate transport base, each auditable transportation adjustment, and the final total; the admin booking page links to it and exposes the same breakdown. Evidence: prior focused price suite passed 108 tests / 1,310 assertions with EN/AR browser coverage; new transport/invoice Pest passed 2 tests / 13 assertions, including Brick Money totals, printed transport lines and source audit records. Pint and `git diff --check` passed. No PDF or tax-authority integration is claimed; the invoice output is the verified HTML print surface. The repaired full-marketplace browser journey passed; final local matrix evidence is recorded below.

records.title: P1 — Replace obsolete rental fields with dimensions.
records.body: Added nullable length_m, width_m and height_m to the existing rental-detail table through an additive migration; the explicit unit is metres and values roundtrip as two-decimal strings. Unknown historical dimensions stay null, never inferred from minimum floor space. Rental vendor create/edit forms now expose EN/AR Length, Width and Height instead of teardown, deposit and minimum-space inputs. Removed legacy fields are also excluded from vendor-page payloads, so normal saves and injected stale form state cannot erase historical values. records.title: TA-SYS-001 — Published service returned as unavailable in wishlist
records.body:
Severity: medium. Save the published sale fixture to `POST /api/v1/customer/wishlist/items`. Creation returns 201 and the correct public service ID, but `data.is_available` is false. The same service is published, stocked and displayable in discovery.

Root cause: `app/Modules/Discovery/Http/Resources/WishlistItemResource.php:24` compares `Service.status` directly to the `ServiceStatus::Published` enum. `Service.php:106` casts the status to `ServiceState`, so the strict comparison fails.

Repro: `tests/tester-army/bugs/wishlist-availability.e2e.ts`. Evidence: `.e2e/system-audit/repros/results/wishlist-availability-published-displayable-service-10555c5fea52f710/trace.md`.

records.title: TA-SYS-002 — Accepted chat report type reaches an unhandled server exception
records.body:
Severity: medium. An authenticated customer submits `reportable_type=chat_thread`, a valid-format public ULID that does not exist, `reason=other` and local test details. The expected outcome is a client error for the unsupported/missing target. Actual status is **500**, captured by the repeat assertion `expected 500 to be less than 500`.

Root cause: `app/Modules/TrustSafety/Http/Requests/SubmitReportRequest.php:24` accepts `chat_thread`, while `SubmitReportAction.php:17` maps only `vendor_profile` and line 28 throws `InvalidArgumentException` for the accepted chat type. This confirms an input-handling failure, not a successful test of reports against real chat participants.

Repro: `tests/tester-army/bugs/report-type.e2e.ts`. Evidence: `.e2e/system-audit/repros/results/report-type-unknown-chat-report-target-91b3566f01d265d5/trace.md`.

records.title: 01 — One gallery source and actual storage checks
records.body:
`VendorBrowsingRepository::portfolioFor()` previously aggregated only service images while the Blade controller read vendor-owned portfolio media. They now share one ordered source: vendor portfolio first, then galleries of displayable vendor-owned services. URLs are deduplicated. The existing API limit remains 24 while the web gallery can reach all valid images; `total_count` measures all valid unique images.

`PublicMediaUrl::for()` checks the configured conversion disk for a generated conversion, then the original disk. Missing conversions fall back to existing originals; missing media is excluded without fabricating images or deleting data. The generic service card uses the same safe selection for its medium image. Runtime failures in the vendor gallery skip the failed image and reveal an empty state when none remain. Broken thumbnails are hidden.

Files: `app/Modules/Shared/Application/Services/PublicMediaUrl.php`, `app/Modules/Discovery/Infrastructure/Repositories/VendorBrowsingRepository.php`, `app/Modules/Discovery/Http/Controllers/Web/VendorController.php`, `resources/views/storefront/vendors/show.blade.php`, `resources/js/storefront.js`, `resources/views/components/storefront/service-card.blade.php`, `lang/{en,ar}/storefront.php`.

Storage limitation: this checkout has a copied `public/storage` directory rather than a link. Browser setup copies only its own synthetic QA SVG assets to the corresponding public paths, preserving the directory. Production must serve originals and conversions from the configured public disk/storage URL. PHP disk existence does not prove CDN access; post-deployment HTTP verification remains necessary. Unrecoverable missing originals require a backup/re-upload on the real server. Runtime recovery prevents broken icons but cannot recover lost bytes.
